summary: Phase 12.1 complete. THE SECOND HARD SITE HELD, AND MORE CHEAPLY THAN THE FIRST: not one proof step of negFixListFaithful_iff changed. The entire code-bearing delta inside the theorem is the binder type, four dropped .toHasFaithfulDedekindINF suffixes, and two kplusLeftBlock_holds -> kplusOpenLeftBlock_holds rewrites; the two-arm rcases on the carrier, the carrier-free by_cases wrapping it, the Ai/Bi split, the vecPinnedConjAll DNF and the x<=r / x=r / x<r peel are all textually unchanged. Scoped build green on the FIRST attempt, zero failed proof attempts, no proof-search tool invoked at any point. The chartered R11 fallback was NOT triggered. Literature was read VERBATIM from the PDF (pp.10-11) before transcribing; the re-base is grounded on Rabinovich's own Case 3 parenthetical on p.10, now quoted in the module docstring. Case 1's gate re-pointed kplusLeftBlock -> kplusOpenLeftBlock; witness_absurd_of_kplusLeft and negFixListFaithful_case1_is_indispensable both RE-POINTED to kplusOpen with per-declaration reasons recorded in their docstrings; the _of_attained shim re-routed through HasAttainedINF.toHasFaithfulDedekindINF. Declaration inventory byte-identical in both touched modules (0 additions / 0 removals / 0 renames). Full lake build green (1920 jobs), no new sorries, no new axioms, all three canaries unchanged, EANegationFix/ byte-identical. ONE PLAN ITEM COULD NOT BE EXECUTED (D7) because its premise is factually false about a frozen asset -- reported here, not silently skipped.

hard_site_verdict.detail: Under HasFaithfulDedekindINF the recursion's gate structure is UNCHANGED: `by_cases hsev` (carrier-free, the paper's Case 2 against the rest) wrapping `rcases h_INF.first_occ_tp s.neg z0 z1 h_lt <w,...> with hk | <r0, hr00, hr01, h_none, h_disj>` -- exactly TWO arms, no third disjunct, no endpoint by_cases, no added hypothesis. Inside Case 3, the Ai/Bi split via bracketOf_splitsAt_iff, the head-item vs split-entry-item analysis, and the three-way rcases on list membership are textually untouched. The soundness direction's bracketOne_witness_le_infPin confinement step is carrier-free and unchanged.
hard_site_verdict.why_it_held_not_luck: Grounded on a verbatim re-read of PDF p.10's Case 3 parenthetical: 'If not-K+(not-b1) holds at z0 and there is x in (z0,z1) such that not-b1(x), then such r0 exists because we deal with Dedekind complete chains.' Contrapositively an occurrence yields K+(not-b1)(z0) OR the pin -- a DICHOTOMY at Rabinovich's conjunct-free K+, which is character-for-character HasFaithfulDedekindINF.first_occ_tp. Under the tree's kplus the enumeration is not exhaustive (the extra not-b1(z0) conjunct forces a fourth disjunct the paper has no case for). Now transcribed into the module docstring with the quotation, not asserted.
hard_site_verdict.why_cheaper_than_phase_12: Phase 12 had to move two DEFINITIONS to the source's operator (negFixOneCase1 and infPinPoint) and absorb the resulting mirror-image change in its _sound direction. This module reads the endpoint operator in exactly ONE place (Case 1's block) and imports infPinPoint already-moved, so the definition edge cost one identifier and the binder edge cost four suffixes. Nothing else.
hard_site_verdict.scope_limit: This settles the LIST-FORM hard site. Both hard sites named by the plan are now landed. Phase 13 is surveyed as a PURE SIGNATURE SWAP with no destructure sites; that survey is now partially corroborated (this phase touched two of Phase 13's sites mechanically and neither needed proof work) but the survey's claim of 'six hypothesis sites, no destructure sites' was NOT independently re-verified here.

deviations.plan_item: Phase 12.1 task: 'Remove D4's kplusOpen_of_kplus at :468. Unlike D3's four coercions the build will NOT enforce this one -- the weakening stays type-correct under either carrier.'
deviations.what_is_false: The item treats the coercion as an artifact of the mixed carrier that the re-base retires. It is not. It is STRUCTURALLY REQUIRED under EITHER carrier, and removing it makes the build RED.
deviations.evidence: HasFaithfulDedekindINF.first_occ (KPlusFaithful.lean:325-331) weakens only its LEFT disjunct to kplusOpen. Its RIGHT disjunct deliberately retains the tree's kplus at r0, and the structure's own docstring at KPlusFaithful.lean:302-305 records this as intentional: the right disjunct is kept 'literally HasDedekindINF's, kplus included' so that 'the two carriers' right disjuncts stay syntactically identical for the re-base.' Since infPinPoint carries the source's conjunct-free kplusOpen, the one-token weakening is needed at the pin regardless of the bound carrier. Phase 12 kept the IDENTICAL coercion at the IDENTICAL spot (NegFixOneFaithful.lean:583) for the IDENTICAL reason and documented it there.
deviations.action_taken: Coercion retained. The five-line SCHEDULED FOR REMOVAL comment replaced by an eleven-line comment explaining with citations why it is permanent. Plan file checklist item left UNCHECKED and annotated with the full diagnosis.
deviations.why_not_BLOCKED: Nothing is ambiguous, nothing is unproved, no settled design was reopened, and the phase's Done-when is otherwise fully met with a green sorry-free axiom-clean build. deviations.why: Unlike Phase 12's D5 (HasDedekindINF/HasFaithfulDedekindINF.first_occ_tp, which are INCOMPARABLE and so were landed additively), these two are COMPARABLE: the kplusOpen form implies the kplus form by kplusOpen_of_kplus, so retaining the old one would duplicate rather than preserve content. For negFixListFaithful_case1_is_indispensable there is a second, stronger reason: it is the non-vacuity artifact certifying that the Case 1 disjunct ACTUALLY PRESENT in the definition cannot be absorbed by its neighbours. Left at kplus it would still compile while silently certifying a gate the definition no longer has -- precisely the failure mode the declaration exists to prevent. Both decisions are recorded in the declarations' own docstrings as the plan directed.

transitive_cascade.warning_performance: Phase 12's generalized two-edge warning was CORRECT and is now confirmed by a second independent instance. This time BOTH edges fired, in the SAME downstream module, in Phase 13's own territory. The binder edge produced an argument-position coercion the build WILL retire when Phase 13 swaps :105's binder (marked SCHEDULED FOR REMOVAL). The definition edge produced an identifier change the build DID enforce. REFINEMENT of the warning: the 'build will not enforce it' hazard is specific to argument-position TYPE weakenings, not to definition moves generally -- when a definition move changes an IDENTIFIER that downstream proofs name, the build catches it.
transitive_cascade.standing_note_for_phase_13: Phase 13 owns VecEANegFixFaithful.lean (plan cites sites :105, :138, :207, :234, shim :312). LINE NUMBERS HAVE SHIFTED by roughly +14 in that file. When Phase 13 swaps :105's binder the :109 coercion disappears automatically. Phase 13 should ALSO re-point VecEA2.negFixFaithful_carries_limit_gate's `hk : kplus` hypothesis to kplusOpen -- deliberately left alone here as out-of-territory. That statement is still TRUE and still load-bearing (kplus -> kplusOpen), but it now certifies the limit gate at a hypothesis one conjunct stronger than the gate negFixListFaithful actually carries, which is the same defect D10 re-pointed away from in negFixListFaithful_case1_is_indispensable. An in-file note records this.
